previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of diabetes, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, Crohn’s disease, and prior right knee replacement presented with dizziness and hypotension. She was found to have leukocytosis and acute kidney injury likely secondary to hypoperfusion. Empiric antibiotics were started for possible sepsis, though blood cultures remained negative and no infectious source was confirmed. Her knee wound showed staphylococcus aureus sensitive to treatment, but no deep joint infection was found. She improved with fluid resuscitation and pressor support, which was weaned off. Her renal function gradually improved, and she did not require transfusion for anemia. She was diagnosed with a right ankle sprain after a fall, with no fracture. Medications were adjusted, including lowering valsartan and switching to metoprolol tartrate. She was discharged home with services in good condition after a four-day stay.

radiology_notes.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST AND RECONSTRUCTIONS.

INDICATION:  History of Crohn's disease with left lower quadrant pain.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axially-acquired images were obtained from the lung bases to
the symphysis after the uneventful intravenous administration of 130 ml
Optiray 350 contrast material.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained
and reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST AND RECONSTRUCTIONS:  Bibasilar atelectasis is
present within the lung bases.  Calcifications within the coronary arteries
and aortic valve are of unknown hemodynamic significance.  No pericardial
effusion.

Ill-defined regions of hyperenhancement within the liver are nonspecific and
may represent hemangiomas or ___.  The gallbladder, spleen, stomach, and
abdominal large and small bowel appear unremarkable.  There is pancreatic
ductal dilatation to 5 mm without focal mass lesion detected within the
pancreatic head.  The adrenal glands appear within normal limits.  The kidneys
enhance and secrete symmetrically.  Hypoattenuating foci are subcentimeter in
bilateral cortices and too small to adequately characterize.  No free fluid or
free air present within the abdomen.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST AND RECONSTRUCTIONS:  The colon is noted with
intraluminal VoLumen and stool with hyperenhancement of the mucosa involving
the cecum.  Minimal surrounding inflammatory change detected with ileocolic
lymph nodes, not pathologically enlarged per CT size criteria.  Equivocal wall
thickening is present within a loop of small bowel within the right lower
quadrant.  No fistulas or intra-abdominal fluid collection is detected.
Moderate calcified atherosclerotic plaque is present within the abdominal
aorta and iliac branches without aneurysmal dilatation.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST AND RECONSTRUCTIONS:  The bladder is moderately
distended without focal lesion detected within.  The rectum, sigmoid colon,
and small bowel loops within the pelvis are within normal limits.  No inguinal
or pelvic adenopathy per CT size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions detected.
Multilevel degenerative changes in the lower lumbar spine.  Sacroiliac joint
degenerative changes with subchondral sclerosis.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Mild mucosal hyperenhancement with minimal surrounding inflammatory
stranding involving the cecum suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease. No
abscess or collection.
2.  Increased pancreatic ductal dilatation from prior studies without
detectable ampullary lesion on this modality.  Finding should be further
evaluated with MRCP vs ERCP.
3.  Ill-defined regions of hyperenhancement within the liver, not fully
characterized, may represent areas of fat sparing.  Finding could be further
evaluated on subsequent MRI/MRCP.

STUDY:  MRCP.

HISTORY:  ___ female with history of Crohn's disease presenting with
epigastric and abdominal pain found to have pancreatic ductal dilatation on
recent CT in addition to ill-defined hyperdensities within the liver.

Further characterization requested.

COMPARISONS:  CT on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1 and T2-weighted images were acquired on a 1.5 Tesla
magnet, including dynamic 3D imaging.  The patient declined intravenous
Gadolinium administration.  Oral administration of contrast included 300 cc of
the Gastromark and 450 ml of RediCAT.

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reformations were generated on an independent work
station.

FINDINGS:  A small amount of linear atelectasis is present at the right lung
base.  Ill-defined areas of increased signal intensity are evident on T2-
weighted imaging throughout the liver including segment VIII  (5:10), segment
V  (5:22), peripherally within segment VI (5:26) and segment IIIIA/V (5:17).
In and out of phase imaging demonstrates no corresponding areas of focal fat
deposition. Given the lack of arterial phase imaging/intravenous contrast
administration, the presence of arterial lesions cannot be assessed. The
biliary system appears normal.

The gallbladder, spleen, adrenal glands, kidneys, and visualized stomach,
large and small bowel appear unremarkable.

The pancreas is mildly atrophic in appearance.  The pancreatic duct is
diffusely dilated measuring up to 4.7 mm in diameter and several dilated ducts
are evident likely representing sequelae from chronic pancreatitis (series 8,
image 3).

There is no free intra-abdominal fluid.  No osseous lesions are present.

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reformations provided multiple perspectives for the
dynamic series.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Limited study given lack of intravenous contrast.  Ill-defined areas of
diffuse signal abnormality throughout the liver, incompletely characterized by
MRI.

2.  4.7 mm dilated pancreatic duct with associated prominent side branches,
most likely representing chronic pancreatitis. Evaluation for underlying mass
is somewhat limited by lack of IV contrast.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with Crohn's disease and left flank pain. Evaluate
for stone.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast CT abdomen/pelvis ___.

KUB, SUPINE VIEW ONLY:  Evaluation of the kidneys is limited by overlying
bowel gas.  No renal or ureteral stones are identified.  

There are non-dilated loops of small bowel containing residual oral contrast,
and non-dilated loops of gas filled small bowel and colon.

IMPRESSION:  Limited evaluation of the kidneys due to overlying bowel gas.

Please note that, on review of the noncontrast CT abdomen/pelvis of ___, no renal or ureteral stones are identified.
